overwrite_safety_analysis.question: Is it safe for the pipeline to overwrite manual README edits with full-replacement renders?
evidence: 1. Both manual edits (Words 14e3eb8, PDF e49ea8a) added example table rows and directory tree entries — the same data the pipeline generates programmatically.
2. The pipeline README includes all examples the manual edits added, PLUS additional examples from PR packages not yet merged, PLUS full source code snippets in collapsible sections.
3. The manual edits contain no unique prose, disclaimers, licensing text, or maintainer notes that would be lost.
4. For Words: the manual edit was already superseded by two subsequent pipeline commits (6a5f20a, 1b9f4e7).
5. For PDF: the manual edit is still HEAD but lists only 5 examples. The cumulative pipeline README lists 17 examples. Overwrite strictly improves coverage.
6. The final README policy is full-replacement (no managed section markers in place). The plan-healing design documents this explicitly and defers marker introduction to a future sprint.
overwrite_safety_analysis.readme_policy: FULL_REPLACEMENT — the pipeline owns the entire README.md content. No managed-section markers are currently in use. This was a conscious design decision documented in manual-readme-preservation-design.json.

conclusion: Manual README edits detected in 2 of 6 repos (Words: 14e3eb8, PDF: e49ea8a). Both edits added missing example entries to the table — the same gap Sprint 34 fixes programmatically. Full replacement is safe because: (a) manual content is a strict subset of pipeline output, (b) Words manual edit already superseded by pipeline, (c) PDF manual edit will be superseded on next publish-readme --publish.
